Diagnostics of several analyses side by side

Source: R/compare.R
compare_profiles.Rd

Collects several posterior fits, sets of draws, profiles or designs, such as the analyses of several outcomes, effect measures or subsets of sites, and tabulates their diagnostics side by side.

Usage

compare_profiles(..., .list = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'profile_comparison'
plot(x, type = NULL, ...)

Arguments

...

For compare_profiles(), named objects of class reliability_posterior, reliability_draws, reliability_profile or reliability_design. For plot(), further arguments of the plot function.

.list

Optionally, a named list of such objects, added after those in ....

x

A comparison made by compare_profiles().

type

The plot of a comparison: "functionals" (the posterior densities of the informativeness, for posterior fits and draws only), "plane", "compare", "profile", "gap" or "concentration". NULL, the default, gives "functionals" when every analysis is a posterior fit or draws, and "compare" otherwise.

Value

An object of class profile_comparison, a list with the components

  • objects: the named list of analyses.

  • table: a data frame with one row per analysis and the columns analysis, source, J, I, I_lower, I_upper, mean, mean_lower, mean_upper, H, H_lower, H_upper, J_eff, V, prob_I_above and sigma_tau (posterior means, or values at a fixed sigma_tau, with the ends of the posterior intervals).

print(), as.data.frame() (the table), profile_summary(), report_table(), report_text() and plot() take it.

Details

The table has one row per analysis with the informativeness, the mean reliability, the dispersion, the concentration count and the logit variance, and their posterior intervals where there are any. The analyses can be of different kinds, which the column source records. Each analysis is conditional on its own standard errors, so analyses of the same sites with different effect measures (a risk difference and a log odds ratio, for example) have different diagnostics.

See also

prior_sensitivity() for the same analysis under several priors, and vignette("multisite-trial") for a comparison of the analyses of one trial.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
prof <- reliability_profile(fit)
cmp <- compare_profiles(posterior = fit, `plug-in` = prof)
cmp
#> Comparison of 2 analyses
#> Intervals are central posterior intervals.
#> Each analysis is conditional on its own standard errors.
#> 
#>   analysis   J  informativeness I     mean reliability
#>   posterior  8  0.225 [0.000, 0.745]  0.230
#>   plug-in    8  0.338                 0.346
#> 
#>   analysis   dispersion H             concentration count J_eff
#>   posterior  0.0143 [0.0000, 0.0283]  7.2
#>   plug-in    0.0249                   7.4
